mainTopic: Is a מופלא סמוך לאיש an adult by Torah law or only by rabbinic law, for vows, הקדש and תרומה?
overview: The amud starts with a ברייתא. It says the Torah treats a מופלא סמוך לאיש like an adult for oaths and vows, but he does not bring a קרבן for misusing his own הקדש. The גמרא tries to prove from it that such a minor gets lashes, but rereads the wording. After a few attempts, it concludes that his vow binds only מדרבנן, and the פסוק is just an אסמכתא. Then it examines the dispute between רב כהנא and רבי יוחנן with ריש לקיש about others eating a minor's הקדש. It traces the dispute to whether a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by Torah law or only by rabbinic law. רב ירמיה challenges the Torah-law view from an orphan girl whose rabbinic-level husband cancels her vow. The גמרא defends it with שמואל's 'either way' answer, רבה בר ליואי's ongoing cancellation, and רבא's rule that a wife vows with her husband's consent in mind. Finally, אביי tries a proof from רבי יוסי's ruling on a minor's תרומה. That leads to a debate over whether רבי יוסי holds that תרומה nowadays is Torah law. The amud ends just as the גמרא begins a supporting ברייתא about dough mixed with תרומה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא: should the minor also bring a קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that the Torah treats a near-adult minor like an adult for oaths and vows. So maybe he should also bring a קרבן for misusing his own consecrated item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we find that the Torah treats the minor like an adult for breaking an oath on purpose, for vows of prohibition, and for 'he shall not break his word,' maybe he should also have to bring a קרבן for misusing his own הקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא starts with what we already know and then raises a possible extension. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The starting point is that a מופלא סמוך לאיש counts as an adult in three areas: זדון שבועה, איסר, and בל יחל. The ברייתא suggests this might carry over to מעילה, so that he would bring a קרבן if he used his own הקדש. The word יכול tells us this is only a first thought, which the ברייתא is about to reject.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor close to adulthood who understands what a vow means
Breaking an oath on purpose
A vow that makes something forbidden to oneself
'He shall not break his word,' the לאו against breaking a vow
Property given to the בית המקדש
'One might think.' It introduces a first idea that will be rejected

phrases.english: Since we find that the verse equated
the minor to the adult regarding an intentional oath
phrases.notes: 'The minor' here means the sharp minor just before adulthood, not any small child.

phrases.english: and regarding a vow of prohibition, and regarding 'he shall not break [his word],'
one might think he should be liable
to bring an offering for [misusing] his consecrated property?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהֵא חַיָּיב עַל הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹ קׇרְבָּן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the minor's adult status for vows also make him bring a קרבן for misusing his own הקדש?

steps.title: 'זה הדבר' limits it to vows
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק 'זה הדבר': the minor counts as an adult only for vows, not for a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'This is the matter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea from step 1 by quoting the פסוק 'זה הדבר.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'this' limits the rule. Only in the area of vows is the near-adult minor treated like an adult, so he does not bring a קרבן for misusing his own הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches.' It introduces the source that settles the question
'This is the matter,' read here as a limiting word

phrases.english: The verse states: 'This is the matter.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. 'זה הדבר' limits his adult status to vows only, so there is no קרבן.

steps.title: Proof that the minor is liable for בל יחל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא calls the minor 'liable' for איסר and בל יחל. That suggests he gets lashes, which supports רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, it teaches that for a vow of prohibition and for 'he shall not break his word' he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the ברייתא's wording. It reads 'liable' as meaning real punishment, which would back up רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיהת means 'leave the main topic aside and look at this detail.' The ברייתא lists בל יחל as its own item and uses the word חייב. That sounds like the minor is fully liable for the לאו, which means מלקות. This fits רב הונא's view that such a minor who eats food he consecrated gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In any event, it teaches.' It points to a detail of the source as proof
Liable, here understood as liable for punishment

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches
that regarding a vow of prohibition and regarding 'he shall not break [his word]' he is liable.

steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that a מופלא סמוך לאיש gets lashes
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists 'and בל יחל' as its own item and calls him 'liable'

steps.title: Reread: only 'the איסור of בל יחל'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. It suggests reading the words as 'the איסור of בל יחל,' meaning a prohibition with no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'regarding the prohibition of he shall not break his word.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 3 by suggesting a slightly different reading of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take away the 'and' between the two items. Then the ברייתא only says that an איסור of בל יחל applies to him. It no longer says he is liable for lashes, so the proof for רב הונא is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say instead.' It offers a different reading
A prohibition, here meaning one without lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up אִיסָּר (a vow of prohibition, step 1) with אִיסּוּר (a prohibition in general). The new reading turns them into one phrase: 'the איסור of בל יחל.'

phrases.english: Say: 'regarding the prohibition of "he shall not break [his word]."'

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ברייתא's wording, not רב הונא's view itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as giving only an איסור, not lashes

steps.title: Either way, an איסור without lashes makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how there can be an איסור without lashes. If the minor is an adult by Torah law he should get lashes, and if he isn't, there should be no איסור at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prohibition of 'he shall not break his word'? Either way it's a problem: if the near-adult minor counts by Torah law, he should get lashes too. And if he doesn't count by Torah law, there is no prohibition either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading from step 4 with a 'whichever way you look at it' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 left the minor in a middle position: he has an איסור but no lashes. The גמרא shows that this middle position doesn't hold up. If he counts as an adult מדאורייתא, breaking a לאו brings lashes. If he doesn't count, the Torah's לאו doesn't apply to him at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whichever way you want.' Both options lead to a problem
By Torah law
He should get lashes too

phrases.english: The prohibition of 'he shall not break [his word]'? Whichever way you take it:
if the sharp minor near adulthood [counts as an adult] by Torah law,
he should also be flogged;
and if the sharp minor near adulthood
is not [an adult] by Torah law,
there is no prohibition either.

steps.kashyaTarget: The rereading in step 4 (איסור without lashes)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah איסור either applies, and then brings lashes, or doesn't apply at all. There is no middle position for the minor himself.

steps.title: The איסור is on the adults who are warned about him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the איסור is not on the minor himself. It is on the people who are warned to keep him away from what he forbade.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The prohibition applies] to those who are warned about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. The 'איסור' in the ברייתא is placed on others, not on the minor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 5 assumed the איסור was on the minor himself. The answer moves it to the people responsible for him, who must keep him away from the forbidden item. So the minor gets no lashes, and the reading from step 4 still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who are warned about him, meaning responsible for keeping him away

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove רב הונא's view. It can be read as an איסור of בל יחל that falls on the adults around the minor, with no lashes for the minor himself.

phrases.english: To those who are warned regarding him.
phrases.notes: This means the adults who must keep the minor away from the item he forbade.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes who the איסור applies to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The איסור is on the minor himself, which leads to the 'either way' problem
steps.terutzMaskana: The איסור is on the people warned about him, so the minor gets no lashes and the rereading stands

steps.title: Does this mean a court must stop a minor from eating forbidden food?
steps.stepSummary: If others must keep the minor away from what he forbade, it seems a court must stop a minor from eating נבלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: if a minor eats נבלות, the court is commanded to stop him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls a troubling conclusion out of the answer in Step 6. It treats that conclusion as a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said adults must keep the minor away from the thing he forbade. If that is so, it would follow that a court must stop any minor from eating forbidden food like נבלות. The גמרא treats this as a problem, because elsewhere this is not a settled rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude from here
Meat of animals that died without proper שחיטה
The court
To separate him, meaning to stop him from the forbidden thing

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a rule the גמרא accepts. It is an unwanted result of the last answer, and the next step works to avoid it.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
a minor who eats carcass meat —
the court is commanded to stop him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 6 by showing where it leads
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the איסור falls on others who must keep the minor away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If others must keep him away, then a court must stop a minor from eating any forbidden food, which is not a settled rule

steps.title: The case is where the minor made it הקדש and others ate it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means that adults are forbidden to eat what the minor made הקדש. It says nothing about stopping the minor himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? Where he made it הקדש, and others ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows Step 6's answer. The איסור is on other people eating what the minor made הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'others' are not being told to stop the minor. They themselves may not eat the food he made holy. So we learn nothing about a court stopping a minor from eating forbidden food.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? A way of narrowing the case
He made it holy, set aside for the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
Where he himself made it holy,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the minor. He set the food aside as הקדש.

phrases.english: and others ate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The others must stop the minor himself from eating
steps.terutzMaskana: The others are forbidden to eat what the minor made הקדש

steps.title: This only works for the view that others get lashes
steps.stepSummary: Step 8 fits רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, who say others get lashes. It does not fit רב כהנא, who says they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says that if he made it הקדש and others ate it, they get lashes. But for the one who says they do not get lashes, what can be said? It was stated: if he made it הקדש and others ate it, רב כהנא says they get no lashes. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say they get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 8. It shows that the answer only works for one side of a dispute between אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב כהנא, eating the minor's הקדש brings no lashes, so it is not a real Torah איסור. Then the ברייתא's 'איסור' cannot be about others eating it. The question 'how can there be an איסור without lashes?' is back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says
What can be said? We have no answer for that view
They get lashes

phrases.english: This works for the one who says:
"If he made it holy and others ate it, they get lashes,"
but for the one who says "they do not get lashes" —
what can be said?
For it was stated: if he made it holy and others ate it,
Rav Kahana says: they get no lashes;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְהוּ: לוֹקִין!
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish both say: they get lashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The narrowed case where others ate the minor's הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב כהנא no lashes come from that case, so it cannot explain the ברייתא's איסור

steps.title: The איסור is only rabbinic and the פסוק is just a support
steps.stepSummary: The minor's vow is binding only by rabbinic law. That is why there is an איסור but no lashes. The פסוק is only a hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is rabbinic, and the פסוק is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question from Step 5. The איסור of בל יחל for this minor is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 asked how there can be an איסור without lashes. The answer: the איסור comes from the רבנן, and lashes come only for Torah איסורים. The ברייתא quoted a פסוק, but that פסוק is only an אסמכתא, a hint for a rabbinic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law
Just a support; a פסוק used as a hint for a rabbinic rule, not as its true source

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer: a minor's vow is binding only מדרבנן. So breaking it is an איסור but brings no lashes, and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא quotes a פסוק, but that does not make the rule Torah law. Here the פסוק is only a hint.

phrases.english: It is rabbinic,
phrases.notes: The גמרא goes back to reading the ברייתא as an איסור on the minor himself, but only from the רבנן.

phrases.english: and the verse is merely a support.
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק the ברייתא leaned on in Step 1 when it said the Torah treats the minor like an adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by dropping the 'others' approach
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the source as rabbinic with an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's פסוק shows the minor is an adult by Torah law
steps.terutzMaskana: The איסור is rabbinic, so there are no lashes; the פסוק is only a hint
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a source can use a פסוק and still describe only a rabbinic law. That idea comes up all over ש״ס.

steps.title: Returning to the dispute about eating a minor's הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the dispute between רב כהנא and רבי יוחנן with ריש לקיש so it can study it on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself: if he made it הקדש and others ate it, רב כהנא says they get no lashes. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say they get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings back the dispute quoted in Step 9 to examine it directly, setting up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the dispute was only a tool to challenge an answer. Now the גמרא wants to understand the dispute itself. This step simply restates both views.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; the גמרא returns to look at a source it quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
if he made it holy and others ate it —
Rav Kahana says: they get no lashes;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: לוֹקִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish both say: they get lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the dispute from Step 9 to study it directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא: no lashes for eating the minor's הקדש; רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: lashes

steps.title: What is the root of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle these אמוראים disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the dispute. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on the facts of the case. The גמרא wants to find the deeper idea that makes one side give lashes and the other not.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? Asking for the root of a dispute

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute stated in Step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that divides רב כהנא from רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש

steps.title: Is a מופלא סמוך לאיש an adult by Torah law or by rabbinic law?
steps.stepSummary: One side holds a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by Torah law, so his הקדש is real and others get lashes. The other side holds it is only rabbinic, so there are no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by Torah law, and one master holds that a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the dispute is about the status of a minor close to adulthood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say his vows and הקדש count by Torah law, so eating his הקדש is a Torah איסור with lashes. רב כהנא says they count only מדרבנן, so there are no lashes. This fits Step 10, which also treated the minor's vow as only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor close to adulthood who understands what a vow means
By Torah law
One master holds

steps.whatToRemember: The whole sugya turns on one question: is a מופלא סמוך לאיש an adult by Torah law (רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש) or only by rabbinic law (רב כהנא)?

phrases.english: One master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, who said there are lashes.

phrases.english: a minor near adulthood counts by Torah law,
and one master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רב כהנא, who said there are no lashes.

phrases.english: a minor near adulthood counts by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: מוּפְלָא סָמוּךְ לְאִישׁ דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree whether a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by Torah law or only by rabbinic law
steps.whyThisMatters: The status of a מופלא סמוך לאיש decides whether his vows and הקדש carry Torah weight, including lashes for anyone who breaks them.

steps.title: An orphan girl's vow and her husband's cancellation
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה quotes a ברייתא: a husband may cancel the vow of a יתומה. That fits the view that a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult only by rabbinic law. It seems to contradict the view that he is an adult by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה objects: An orphan girl who made a vow can have her vow cancelled by her husband. If a מופלא סמוך לאיש counts only by rabbinic law, that makes sense: a rabbinic marriage cancels a rabbinic vow. But if it is Torah law, can a rabbinic marriage cancel a Torah vow?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה attacks the opinion from Step 13 that a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by Torah law. His source is a ברייתא about an orphan girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor orphan girl can only be married off by her mother or brothers, so her marriage is only rabbinic. If her vow is Torah-level, a husband who is only her husband by rabbinic law should not be able to cancel it. So the ברייתא seems to show that her vow is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphan girl, here one with no father, married off as a minor by her mother or brothers
Cancels (a vow), the power a husband has over his wife's vows
A marriage that is valid only by rabbinic law
By Torah law
It makes sense (sets up the case that fits, before the case that does not)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the girl is married. The question is how strong her marriage is (rabbinic only) compared to how strong her vow is.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya objects:
An orphan girl who vowed —
phrases.notes: She is a minor with no father. Her mother or brothers married her off, which is a marriage only by rabbinic law.

phrases.english: her husband may cancel it for her.
It makes sense if you say
a sharp minor near adulthood counts only by rabbinic law;
then a rabbinic marriage comes
and cancels a rabbinic vow.
But if you say it is Torah law,
can a rabbinic marriage come
and cancel a Torah vow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the Torah-law side of the dispute explained in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic-level marriage should not have the power to cancel a Torah-level vow, yet the ברייתא says the husband cancels it.

steps.title: Either way the husband may cancel
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the ברייתא works on both views. If the vow is rabbinic, the rabbinic husband cancels it. If it is Torah-level, she is still a minor, and nobody has to stop a minor from sinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Her husband cancels her vow either way. If the vow is rabbinic, the marriage is rabbinic too. If the vow is Torah law, she is like a child eating non-kosher meat, and בית דין does not have to stop him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל defends the Torah-law view. He shows that the ברייתא does not prove anything either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the Torah-law view the cancellation may not really work. But that does no harm, because she is still a minor. A minor who breaks a prohibition is not someone בית דין must stop, so the husband's cancellation is allowed to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it; both possibilities lead to the same result
A minor who eats non-kosher animal meat, the model case for a child doing an איסור
To stop him or keep him away (from a sin)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that בית דין does not have to stop a minor from sinning lets the גמרא avoid the contradiction without deciding the dispute.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Her husband cancels for her, whichever way you look at it:
if the vow is rabbinic, the marriage is rabbinic too;
if it is Torah law —
it is a case of a minor eating non-kosher meat,
phrases.notes: He means that even if her vow is still binding, she is a child breaking an איסור, like a child eating נבלות.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בֵּית דִּין מְצוִּּוין עָלָיו לְהַפְרִישׁוֹ.
phrases.english: and the court is not commanded to stop him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ירמיה's objection in Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: ממה נפשך: the ruling holds under both views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves the vow must be only rabbinic
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if the vow is Torah-level, letting a minor rely on a weak cancellation is fine, because no one must stop a minor from sinning

steps.title: What happens when she grows up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: once she becomes an adult, she will keep eating what she forbade on herself. She relies on the first cancellation, which did not work by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when she grows up, she will eat based on the first cancellation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's answer by looking ahead to when the girl becomes an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's answer only covers the time she is a minor. Once she is an adult, she really is breaking a Torah vow, and adults must be stopped. Her first cancellation was weak, so the problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: She grew up (reached adulthood)
The first cancellation, the one made while she was a minor

phrases.english: But when she grows up,
she will eat, relying on the first cancellation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reasoning that a minor need not be stopped
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reasoning ends once she becomes an adult, but she keeps relying on a cancellation that never worked by Torah law.

steps.title: The husband keeps cancelling at every moment
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר ליואי answers that the husband cancels her vows at every moment. So when she becomes an adult, a real cancellation takes effect. This works only if he lived with her after she grew up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר ליואי said: Her husband cancels for her at every single moment, and this is where he had relations with her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר ליואי answers the question about what happens when she grows up. The next step challenges his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's cancellation is not a single act in the past. It is treated as ongoing. Once he lives with her as an adult, the marriage becomes Torah-level. Then his ongoing cancellation works by Torah law too.

keyTerms.meaning: Every single moment, again and again
That he had marital relations with her (here, after she became an adult)

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbinic husband can cancel a young orphan wife's vow either way (ממה נפשך). Once she grows up, the cancellation keeps going, and it works by Torah law once he has lived with her as an adult.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Livai said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּעְלָהּ מֵפֵר לָהּ כׇּל שָׁעָה וְשָׁעָה,
phrases.english: Her husband cancels for her at every single moment,
and that is where he had relations with her.
phrases.notes: He means relations after she grew up. That makes the marriage Torah-level, so his cancellation now counts by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעְלָהּ מֵפֵר לָהּ כׇּל שָׁעָה וְשָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the cancellation as ongoing, adding a condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her adult self relies on a cancellation made while she was a minor, which was weak
steps.terutzMaskana: The cancellation renews at every moment. Once he lives with her as an adult, it works by Torah law.

steps.title: A husband cannot cancel vows made before the marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה בר ליואי's answer. By Torah law the marriage only begins when she becomes an adult, so her earlier vow came before the marriage, and a husband cannot cancel those.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a husband cannot cancel vows that came before the marriage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 17. Even if the husband keeps cancelling once she grows up, the vow itself was made before their Torah-level marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, she only becomes his real wife when she is an adult. Her vow was made while she was a minor, so it counts as a vow from before the marriage. A husband has no power over those earlier vows, so his later cancellation should not work.

keyTerms.meaning: cancels (a vow)
earlier ones; vows made before the marriage
husband

phrases.english: But a husband cannot cancel earlier vows!
phrases.notes: Earlier here means vows she made before she was his wife by Torah law, while she was still a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of רבה בר ליואי in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the husband's ongoing cancellation takes effect once she becomes an adult.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her vow came before the Torah-level marriage, and a husband cannot cancel vows from before the marriage.

steps.title: Every woman vows with her husband's approval in mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers using רב פנחס in the name of רבא: every woman who vows does so depending on her husband's consent. So even her early vow was tied to him from the start, and he can cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רב פנחס in the name of רבא, who said: any woman who makes a vow makes it with her husband's consent in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The vow was conditional on the husband's approval from the beginning, so he can cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the vow came before the Torah-level marriage. רב פנחס teaches that a wife's vow always has a built-in condition: it holds only if her husband agrees. She was already married to him by rabbinic law, so the vow was tied to him, and his cancellation works even by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman who makes a vow
depending on her husband's consent

steps.whatToRemember: A wife's vow always carries an unspoken condition that her husband agrees. That is why the husband in our case can cancel even a vow she made as a minor.

phrases.english: It is like the teaching of Rav Pinchas in the name of Rava,
for Rav Pinchas said in the name of Rava:
Any woman who makes a vow
makes the vow with her husband's consent in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces an outside principle that changes how the vow is understood.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow was a separate vow from before the marriage, beyond the husband's power.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her vow was conditional on her husband's consent from the start, so he can cancel it.

steps.title: אביי brings a משנה about a minor separating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה about a boy without two hairs who separates תרומה. רבי יהודה says it never counts. רבי יוסי says it counts once he reaches the age of vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear: a minor who has not grown two hairs — רבי יהודה says his תרומה is not תרומה. רבי יוסי says: before he reaches the age of vows, his תרומה is not תרומה; once he reaches the age of vows, his תרומה is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new attempt to settle the question from earlier: is a מופלא סמוך לאיש an adult by Torah law or by rabbinic law? Here he just quotes the source; the next step explains how it proves something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'age of vows' is exactly the stage of מופלא סמוך לאיש, the year before adulthood. רבי יוסי says a boy at that stage can make real תרומה. The גמרא will now try to use this to show that this stage counts as adult by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: two hairs; the physical sign of adulthood
the portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן
the age of vows; the year just before adulthood

phrases.english: Abaye said: Come and hear:
A minor who has not grown two hairs,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
His terumah is not terumah.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Until he reaches the age of vows
his terumah is not terumah;
once he has reached the age of vows,
his terumah is terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new proof on the main question from step 13, after the vow discussion ended.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תרומות about a minor's תרומה, the view of רבי יוסי.

steps.title: How the תרומה case seems to prove Torah-level adulthood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes רבי יוסי holds that תרומה nowadays is Torah law. Only someone who is an adult by Torah law could fix produce that is טבל by Torah law. So the boy at the age of vows must be an adult by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that רבי יוסי holds תרומה nowadays is Torah law. If a מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by Torah law, fine: a Torah-level man fixes Torah-level טבל. But if he is only an adult by rabbinic law, how can a rabbinic-level man fix Torah-level טבל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how אביי's משנה proves the point. It is built on an assumption about how רבי יוסי views תרומה today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the produce is forbidden by Torah law, only a Torah-level act can make it allowed. A boy who is an adult only by rabbinic law could not remove a Torah prohibition. Since רבי יוסי says his תרומה works, he must be an adult by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: they assumed
תרומה in our times (after the Temple's destruction)
טבל; produce not yet tithed, forbidden to eat
fixes; makes the produce allowed to eat

steps.confusionAlert: The whole proof stands on the assumption at the start ('סַבְרוּהָ'). If רבי יוסי holds that תרומה today is only rabbinic, the proof falls apart, and that is exactly what happens next.

phrases.english: They assumed that Rabbi Yosei holds:
Terumah nowadays is from the Torah.
It works well if you say
that a minor close to adulthood is an adult by Torah law:
then a man by Torah law comes
and fixes untithed produce that is forbidden by Torah law.
But if you say he is an adult only by rabbinic law,
can a man by rabbinic law come
and fix untithed produce that is forbidden by Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה from step 20 proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: A מופלא סמוך לאיש is an adult by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ruling, read with the assumption that תרומה nowadays is Torah law.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי holds תרומה nowadays is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe רבי יוסי holds that תרומה nowadays is only rabbinic, so a rabbinic-level adult can fix it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רבי יוסי holds that תרומה nowadays is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down אביי's proof by changing the assumption it was built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תרומה today is only rabbinic, the produce is only rabbinically forbidden. Then a boy who is an adult only by rabbinic law is good enough to fix it. So the משנה fits both views and proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: from the Rabbis, not from the Torah

phrases.english: No, Rabbi Yosei holds:
Terumah nowadays is only rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי יוסי holds תרומה nowadays is Torah law; he may hold it is rabbinic.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי really hold that תרומה nowadays is rabbinic?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the rejection. It begins quoting a ברייתא from סדר עולם (a work linked with רבי יוסי) that uses a פסוק about returning to the land. That source seems to show that תרומה nowadays is Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold that תרומה nowadays is rabbinic? But it is taught in סדר עולם: "that your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 22. It starts quoting a source that seems to show רבי יוסי holds otherwise. The quote finishes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection only works if רבי יוסי holds תרומה nowadays is rabbinic. The גמרא brings סדר עולם to show he may hold the opposite. If so, the rejection fails and אביי's proof may come back.

keyTerms.meaning: an early work about the order of history
and you shall possess it (the land)

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold
that terumah nowadays is only rabbinic?
But isn't it taught in Seder Olam:
"That your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it,"
phrases.notes: דברים 30:5. The quote keeps going right after this line.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי תְּרוּמָה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds תרומה nowadays is rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא in סדר עולם, read with a פסוק about inheriting the land, seems to show תרומה nowadays is Torah law.

steps.title: No third possession, and סדר עולם is רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא from סדר עולם ends: there was a first and second possession of the land, but there will be no third. רבי יוחנן says סדר עולם was taught by רבי יוסי. So רבי יוסי should hold that תרומה nowadays is Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Jewish people had a first and a second possession of the land, but they will not have a third. And רבי יוחנן said: Who taught סדר עולם? רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in step 23. It shows that the source saying תרומה is Torah law nowadays comes from רבי יוסי himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is never a need for a third possession, then the second holiness from עזרא's time never ended. So the land is still holy by Torah law, and תרומה nowadays is Torah law. Since רבי יוסי taught סדר עולם, the rejection in step 22 seems wrong, and the proof from step 21 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Possession, taking hold of ארץ ישראל, which made the land holy
The first possession (in יהושע's time) and the second (in עזרא's time)
An early work on the history and dates of the Jewish people
Who taught this? A question asking who the author of a teaching is

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two possessions with the two בתי מקדש. The point is about the holiness of the land: the second time it became holy, that holiness stayed, even after the second בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is what puts the proof from step 21 back in play. If רבי יוסי holds תרומה is Torah law, then the boy at the age of vows must be an adult by Torah law.

phrases.english: A first possession and a second —
phrases.notes: These match the two 'possess' words in the פסוק from step 23 (דברים 30:5).

phrases.english: they have,
a third — they do not have.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תְּנָא סֵדֶר עוֹלָם? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: Who taught Seder Olam? Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאן תְּנָא סֵדֶר עוֹלָם? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא started in step 23 and connects it to רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rejection in step 22, which said רבי יוסי may hold that תרומה nowadays is only rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סדר עולם says the second holiness of the land is permanent, which makes תרומה Torah law today. רבי יוסי taught סדר עולם, so he should hold that תרומה is Torah law.

steps.title: רבי יוסי taught it but does not hold it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי passed on the teaching of סדר עולם, but he does not personally agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי taught it, but he does not hold like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rejection from step 22. It says רבי יוסי repeated the teaching of סדר עולם without agreeing with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sage can pass on a teaching he received even if his own view is different. So the fact that רבי יוסי taught סדר עולם does not prove his own view. He can still hold that תרומה nowadays is only rabbinic, and then the proof from step 21 falls again.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it, passed it on as a teaching
But he does not hold like it himself

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei taught it,
but he does not hold like it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְלָא סָבַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 and saves the rejection of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates teaching a source from agreeing with it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוסי taught סדר עולם, he must hold that תרומה nowadays is Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי only passed on the teaching. His own view can still be that תרומה nowadays is rabbinic.

steps.title: Support from dough mixed with תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is reasonable that רבי יוסי does not hold like סדר עולם, and starts to quote a ברייתא about regular dough that got mixed with תרומה dough, or was made to rise with תרומה sourdough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also reasonable to say this, as a ברייתא teaches: Dough that got mixed with תרומה, or that rose from sourdough of תרומה —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for its answer in step 25. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and the ruling will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to show from another source that רבי יוסי really treats תרומה nowadays as rabbinic. The case is regular dough that became מדומע, mixed with תרומה, or rose because of תרומה sourdough. The ruling in this ברייתא, and רבי יוסי's view there, will give the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense, a phrase that brings support for the answer just given
Dough
Became מְדוּמָּע, regular food mixed with תרומה
Sourdough used to make dough rise

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable, as it is taught:
Dough that became mixed with תרומה,
or that was leavened with sourdough of תרומה —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי does not hold like סדר עולם, and treats תרומה nowadays as rabbinic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about dough mixed with תרומה or made to rise with תרומה sourdough. Its ruling comes next.
